clinician_items: 31083451: Spontaneous reports of herbal induced liver injury with Petadolex. Causality for 48 cases: 3 likely, 13 possible, 8 unlikely, 24 unclassifiable or unclassified. Nine severe (ALT 3 to 153-fold, AST 2 to 104-fold ULN), average onset 103 days, dose range 50 to 225 mg/day for the mild group. Cases resolved after withdrawal, though two patients required liver transplantation. 22 reported hepatotoxic co-medications. Authors call cases rare, idiosyncratic and frequently confounded. No incidence can be read from this.
39853578: 2025 headache review states butterbur preparations have strong evidence for efficacy and concern for hepatotoxicity, and refers readers to NCCIH.

NCCIH butterbur page (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/butterbur, last updated November 2024, not a PMID): AAN recommended butterbur in 2012 (22529203), then stopped in 2015 because of serious safety concerns. Raw plant contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids; only PA-free products should be considered. Rare liver injury is reported with products said to be PA-free.

35585841: narrative review reporting on Petadolex: no relevant abnormal liver function in its RCTs, and bile duct hyperplasia in rats at 45 to 90-fold of the maximal clinical dose. Counter-evidence from authors reporting their own data; it doesn't address the spontaneous reports in its abstract.
12864764: 2003 report concludes the extract is safe, with no numbers in the abstract. It predates 31083451.

37394426: rats only: two oily PA-free butterbur products raised CYP2B expression above 10-fold with liver enlargement, and one powdery product had no significant effect. Shows products differ; no human finding. Possible CYP interaction question, not established in humans by this paper.
15623680, 14752215, 17659990: mild gastrointestinal events or good tolerability only; none of these abstracts reports liver tests, so they neither support nor refute liver risk.
What I read doesn't establish causation or a rate. It also doesn't show whether the 22 non-Petadolex labels are PA-free.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_strong rests on one RCT (15623680), per-protocol, positive at 150 mg/day and not at 100 mg/day, though the stored dose lists both. Reviews read as moderate (16987643) or positive but limited (32310327); 39853578 says strong. The stored record doesn't separate Petadolex from unbranded labels.
